title: The Smell of Food and Sound of Coin (ಕನ್ನಡ)
summary: A greedy sweetmaker demands payment from a penniless beggar who inhaled the aroma of frying jalebis. Birbal pays the baker with the clinking sound of silver. [KN]
keywords: the smell of food and sound of coin
full_text:
In the bustling sweet bazaar of Agra, a notoriously greedy confectioner named Halwai Mangat Ram fried fresh, golden jalebis and syrup-soaked gulab jamuns in a giant vat of boiling ghee. The sweet, buttery aroma wafted down the alleyway.

A penniless, starving beggar named Ramu stood on the public street outside the shop. Unable to afford even a single morsel, the poor man closed his eyes, inhaled the heavenly fragrance of the hot sweets, and ate his dry piece of stale bread, pretending he was enjoying a royal feast.

Seeing this, Mangat Ram bounded out of his shop with a wooden ladle, grabbed the beggar by the collar, and yelled: 'Pay me ten copper coins at once!'

'For what, master?' the terrified beggar cried. 'I did not touch your sweets!'

'You stood outside my shop for an hour, inhaling the rich aroma of my saffron jalebis!' the confectioner screamed. 'My aroma made your dry bread delicious! The fragrance belongs to my shop! Pay for the smell, or I will have you beaten by the city guards!'

The commotion drew a crowd, and soon the absurd dispute was brought before Emperor Akbar's court. Akbar was disgusted by the shopkeeper's greed, but wondered how to dismiss the case with unassailable wit. He handed the matter to Birbal.

Birbal listened to the confectioner's demand. 'Seth Mangat Ram, you claim that the beggar enjoyed the smell of your sweets, and therefore owes you money?'

'Yes, my lord!' the confectioner beamed. 'Fair payment for fair enjoyment!'

Birbal ordered a brass plate and a purse of twenty silver coins brought from the treasury. Birbal picked up five silver coins, held them high above the brass plate, and dropped them: *Clink-clank-chime!*

The coins bounced on the metal with a bright, musical ring.

Birbal looked at Mangat Ram: 'Did you hear that sound, confectioner?'

'Yes, my lord, loud and clear!'

Birbal gathered the coins and dropped them again: *Clink-clank-chime!*

'Did you hear it again?'

'Yes, wise minister, a beautiful, rich sound!'

Birbal placed the coins back into the velvet purse and handed it to the palace attendant. Turning to the shopkeeper, Birbal said with a serene smile:

'Your debt is settled in full, Mangat Ram. Just as the beggar enjoyed only the aroma of your food without eating a single bite, so too have you enjoyed the musical sound of his money without keeping a single coin! The smell pays for the bread; the chime pays for the smell!'

The courtiers roared with laughter, while Mangat Ram slunk away in red-faced humiliation. Akbar rewarded the beggar with food, praising Birbal's flawless justice.
